title: Fix inconsistent hashing of CallableCustomMethodPointers

milestone.title: 4.x
milestone.description: Issues and pull requests slated for an undetermined Godot 4 release.

body:
## What problem(s) does this PR solve?

- Closes #119740
- Closes #119752
- Closes #89657
- Closes #95512
- Closes #87626
- Reverts #120394

## Additional information
The root cause of these issues is a bug in the hashing of CallableCustomMethodPointers, which meant some HashMap lookups in the connection/disconnection of signals were failing when they should have succeeded. 

#120394 attempted to band-aid over this bug by moving `new` operators out of the memory.h header so they wouldn't be inlined. This probably worked for some configurations, but I was still seeing the bug with gcc 16.2.1 20260810 and lto=full.

The actual bug is `CallableCustomMethodPointerBase::_setup`. The callers of `_setup` would all call it with `_setup((uint32_t *)&data, sizeof(Data));`. That mostly works, but casting `Data*` to `uint32_t*` violates strict aliasing and was technically undefined behavior. Newer versions of gcc with -flto were aggressive enough to take advantage of that UB and were hashing stale/garbage values. It's not actually a GCC bug like #120394 speculated. Since it's technically UB GCC is allowed to do this in its optimization pass.

The fix is changing the signature of `_setup` to take a `std::byte*` instead of `uint32_t*`. Casting a `Data*` to a `std::byte*` (or `char*`, but `std::byte` is more descriptive of what we're doing here) is allowed following strict aliasing. `_setup` then has to put those bytes into a real `uint32_t`, and we've correctly signaled to the compiler what it is we're actually doing: taking the byte representation of `data`, treating it as uint32_t, and hashing.

I think the reason #120394 nudging the compiler to not inline `new` helped is that the main culprit of the bug was that the calls to `_setup` were in constructors, so the compiler wasn't able to catch this "optimization" of hashing garbage instead of `data` when `new` wasn't inlined.  The `std::byte` fix addresses the root cause of the issue, and fixes the issue even when `new` is inlined, so I went ahead and reverted that change. There's no reason we shouldn't be inlining new now that the root cause of the bug is fixed, and as far as I can tell, this bug was the only reason for that change.  If we do want to avoid inlining `new` for some other reason, I'm happy to undo that reversion.
